sections.h2: Who sends a Savannah property tax bill?
sections.html:
A Savannah house is billed twice over. The City of Savannah Revenue Department bills the city tax, and the Chatham County Tax Commissioner bills county, school and other county-level levies. The city's tax calculation page says Savannah residents pay both city and county tax under Georgia law, and school board tax is collected by the county tax commissioner.

  • City of Savannah Revenue Department, 305 Fahm Street, Savannah, GA 31401, 912-651-6455, open Monday to Friday 8:15 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1228, Savannah, GA 31402.
  • Chatham County Board of Assessors, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., Suite 113, 912-652-7271: values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Chatham County Tax Commissioner, 912-652-7100.

The city has no role in setting value. Savannah City Council sets the city millage rate, and the assessors set the value that the rate is applied to.

sections.h2: What does Savannah look like for a property owner?
sections.html:
Savannah covers 106.85 square miles of land and counted 147,780 people in 2020. The Census QuickFacts table puts the July 2025 estimate at 149,440, with 1,383.1 people per square mile.

Owners live in 45.4 percent of homes, so renters are the majority. The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $248,900 and median gross rent is $1,382. There are 58,192 households with a median income of $57,137, and the mean trip to work is 20.7 minutes. Foreign-born residents are 7.6 percent of the population, and 33.3 percent of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree or higher.

That mix of renters, investors and owners gives sellers a wide range of buyers, from owner-occupants to landlords. It also means many parcels are rentals, and rentals are taxed with no homestead relief.

sections.h2: What is the City of Savannah millage rate?
sections.html:
The City of Savannah's July 2026 news release proposed 11.749 mills for 2026, the same as 2025 and what the city calls its lowest rate since 1987. The rollback rate, which would raise the same revenue as the year before, was 11.402 mills.

The county, school board and other levies come on top of the city rate. Exemptions come off assessed value, which is 40 percent of fair market value, before any rate is applied. The city says homes covered by the Stephens-Day exemption are protected from the rise in value that the proposal would otherwise pass on.

sections.h2: When are Savannah property taxes due?
sections.html:
The city bills real property in two installments. The first bills in April and is typically due in mid-June, and it equals half of the prior year's tax. The second bills in September and is typically due in mid-November, and it reflects the current value, exemptions and millage. The city warns that due dates are set when bills are printed and can change.

The county brochure, revised August 14, 2026, states for county bills that the first bill is mailed by April 1 and due June 1, and the second is mailed by September 15 and due November 15. Personal property taxes are due by November 15 each year.

A payment must be received and posted on or before the due date to be on time. The city accepts partial payments up to the second due date, but it does not set up payment arrangements for current or delinquent taxes. Missing a bill does not excuse the tax, and a copy is available online or from the Revenue Department.

sections.h2: What do late Savannah taxes cost?
sections.html:
Delinquent taxes accrue interest at the bank prime rate plus 3 percent a year, calculated monthly, under O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 to 48-2-44. After 120 days a 5 percent penalty is added to all bills except homestead property under $500, and another 5 percent follows each additional 120 days, to a maximum of 20 percent of the tax due.

A fi. fa. is a lien that can hurt the owner's credit and lead to a tax sale. The city holds about six tax sales a year and advertises each property for four weeks beforehand. An owner may redeem within a year and a day by paying the winning bidder the bid plus 20 percent.

If a property is under appeal, the city bills the lesser of the prior year's value or 85 percent of the current value, due on the second installment date. A new bill or refund follows when the appeal is settled.

sections.h2: How do Chatham County's homestead and Stephens-Day exemptions work?
sections.html:
To get the exemption, you must own, occupy and claim the home as your legal residence on January 1. Chatham accepts applications year-round, but one must reach the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the annual notice date to count for that year. Bring a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration at the homestead address, and the assessors may ask for a utility bill or voter card.

  • The regular homestead takes $12,000 off assessed value for county tax and $2,000 off school and state tax.
  • The Stephens-Day exemption, in place since 1999, and the statewide floating exemption freeze the base year value, and the taxpayer gets whichever saves more.
  • The Chatham senior exemption needs the owner to be 65 and net income of $10,000 or less, and takes $30,000 off the county and school assessed value.

A sale, a deed change or major improvements change the base year. The city explains that added value from a bedroom addition goes into the base, and demolition subtracts from it. Opting in or out of HB 581 does not reset a base year. A homestead exemption does not cover solid waste or street light fees.

sections.h2: How does a short-term rental affect a Savannah owner?
sections.html:
Savannah's short-term vacation rental ordinance defines owner-occupied property as a home where the owner lives in the main unit as the primary and usual residence. Proof comes from a valid homestead exemption submitted with the certificate application, or a sworn affidavit plus two proofs of residency.

This ties the exemption to a real residence. An owner who rents out a house and claims homestead there creates a problem when the house is sold, so sort out the exemption status with the assessors first.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Savannah house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Yes. City and county balances are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, once the Revenue Department and the Tax Commissioner supply payoff figures. If the deed has a lien filed, the title work shows it before closing.

A cash purchase avoids a lender appraisal and repair demands. Compare an offer to what a listing would net after repairs, the tax balance and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Who collects City of Savannah property tax?
faqs.a: The City of Savannah Revenue Department collects city tax, at 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455. The Chatham County Tax Commissioner collects the county and school portions.

faqs.q: When is the second Savannah property tax installment due?
faqs.a: It is typically due in mid-November, and the county brochure lists November 15 for county bills. The city sets its dates when it prints bills, so read the due date printed on yours.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Chatham County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the annual notice of assessment, and the appeal goes first to the Chatham County Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Savannah taxes?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at prime plus 3 percent a year applies, and a 5 percent penalty is added after 120 days, repeated every 120 days up to 20 percent.

It is a Chatham County homestead exemption, in place since 1999, that fixes the value used for tax at a base year amount plus improvements. A statewide floating exemption now exists, and the owner gets whichever is larger.
